 (i) There exists a sufficiently large integer $M$ such that $\{b_{n}\}_{n\ge M}$

The additional point in the present note is that the specific lattice $\Z\times \sqrt2\,\Z$ also excludes the remaining $4$-point two-distance configuration consisting of four vertices of a regular pentagon (equivalently, the associated isosceles trapezoid).
